newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Anaheim cuts yields on deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Anaheim cuts yields on deal.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds rose about three-eighths of a point in late trade Tuesday as a dearth of new issues enabled an Anaheim, California, Authority to cut yields and forced buyers into the secondary market.

The recently firmer tone displayed by the Treasury market, which has gained confidence from a series of economic data that suggested the Federal Reserve's policy-making arm likely will leave rates unchanged, has made would-be buyers of municipals reluctant to stay on the sidelines.

"Accounts that have money get nervous," a trader said, explaining that these investors fear yields might keep slipping. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee on Wednesday ends a two-day meeting and most economists look for the body to decide that it need not try to slow the economy by tightening credit.

Despite the interest in buying secondary issues, traders said that fairly few bid-wanted lists were ciruclated. And even with the pick-up in the secondary market, traders cautioned that activity was spotty, and that players still were looking ahead to rising supplies of new issues, which are expected to start hitting the market around mid-February.
At least until then, some issuers are able to take advantage of promising market conditions. "Obviously, any deal being priced is going away, and it's creating quiet a vacuum," the trader said.
California paper, which has been in short supply recently, this week is capturing much of the market's attention with some sizable sales.
Anaheim, Calif.'s Public Financing Authority, which sold $514 million of lease revenue bonds, lowered yields in several maturities, according to the syndicate manager PaineWebber Inc.
For example, the top tax-exempt yield in the offering, which was 5.83 percent in 2037, was lowered to 5.80 percent.

Negotiated offerings for California counties slated for this week include Contra Costa County, Calif., which plans to sell $143 million of revenue bonds, while Riverside County was expected to sell $92 million of revenue bonds.
Competitive offerings for California include $130 million of Fresno Unified School District issues on February 6.
In the secondary market, Houston, Texas, Water and Sewer System Revenues of December 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.75 percent, NET, down one basis point.
And Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of October 2026, which have a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.65 percent, NET, down three basis points.

The March U.S. municipal bonds traded on the Chicago Board of Trade firmed three ticks to 115-30/32, while the March Treasury bond futures rose four ticks to 112-7/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 119 ticks.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales for February 5 are expected to total $291.8 million in 10 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $49.1 million in five sales. The largest is a $21.4 million Somerville, Mass., at 1100 EST.
Negotiated sales total $243 million in five offerings. The largest is a $205 million North Broward Hospital District, Fla., revenue bond offering through Smith Barney Inc.
Day to day muni bond sales total $95 million in two offerings for February 5, which means dealers may bring the offerings to market if conditions warrant.
